We have mass spec data: m/z 194.0862 (intensity 100) as base peak. Likely molecular ion [M+H]+? Usually mass spec ESI positive mode gives [M+H]+. So M = 193.078? Actually m/z 194.086 corresponds to M+H, so neutral mass = 193.078 (approx). The isotopic pattern shows small M+1 (13% intensity) typical for one nitrogen (14N gives +1 ~1%? Actually 13C gives +1 ~1.1% per carbon. For C10, +1 ~11% plus N? So 13% matches C10. So formula likely C10H11NO3? Let's compute exact mass: C10 = 120.000, H11 = 11.086, N = 14.00307, O3 = 47.9847. Sum = 193.0738. Add proton = 194.0815. Our observed 194.0862 close. So formula C10H11NO3 fits.

Now need to determine SMILES. Need to deduce structure from NMR? Not yet measured. Could use search_by_smiles to find similar? But we need propose correct SMILES. Use isomers list from obtain_isomers. Many candidates. Need to narrow using NMR maybe. Let's get carbon and proton NMR spectra for sample (exp).
